title: Photonic Neural Network Processing Unit with Integrated Silicon Photonics
problem: Electronic neural network accelerators suffer from high latency and power consumption when performing matrix multiplications. Achieving both sub-nanosecond latency and low energy consumption remains a key challenge for practical neural network inference.
motivation: Enabling fast, energy-efficient neural network inference is critical for real-time AI applications in data centers and edge devices.
method: The design uses integrated silicon photonics to implement a photonic processing unit that leverages optical parallelism for matrix computations. Photonic circuits exploit wavelength-division multiplexing and parallel optical paths to perform simultaneous operations on neural network data with minimal latency overhead.
key_novelty: Using integrated silicon photonics with optical parallelism to achieve sub-nanosecond latency matrix multiplications for neural networks while consuming 50x less power than electronic implementations.
contributions: Photonic neural network processing unit using integrated silicon photonics
50x power reduction compared to electronic implementations
Demonstration of optical parallelism for neural network acceleration
limitations: Integration challenges with electronic control circuits and scalability to larger network sizes are not discussed.
